window: Written from roughly a year of each account's public posts (107,959 posts across the 38), read on 2026-09-30.

entries.note: First place by a nineteen-vote margin, with fewer followers than almost anyone near her — nine thousand, against Jerry Chen's hundred and thirty and derek guy's six hundred and fifty. She won it in the replies: ninety-one percent of two and a half thousand posts. The feed is a running conversation rather than a broadcast, which is why the grief sits comfortably next to the jokes — cleaning out her office and asking for hugs, three posts from feminising band names into The Vulva Underground. Whatever the leaderboard measures, it isn't reach.
entries.line: if you kiss at Olive Garden is that incest?

entries.note: Second place on 364 posts in eighteen months, which is a third of a post a day, of which ninety-six percent are replies — the highest reply rate on the board. He essentially does not post; he turns up underneath other people and says the thing. The wristlace bit ran for days on pure self-reply, and “unlike you guys, i only suffer from posters gladness” is as close as this list gets to a mission statement.
entries.line: pasta three meals a day is fine if they’re different shapes

entries.note: Three and a half thousand posts, and the striking thing is how wide the register runs. The year's best-performing post is a confessed crush on Michelle Obama; a few weeks either side of it are a note about burying the dog under a black cherry tree, a plea to vote for whoever hurts fewest people, and “If you don't inspect your meat, you can't have any pudding.” Sentiment and filth from the same account, never in the wrong order.
entries.line: Hey wait a minute: maybe the quicksand we grew up worrying about turned out to be our phones

entries.note: Seventeen posts a day and a median of 155 likes, which is the rare combination of volume and hit rate — most people who post this much are shouting into a void. The jokes are compressed to the point of aphorism, and the hardest ones are about her father's dementia, which she writes about with no sentimentality whatsoever and somehow lands as comedy anyway.
entries.line: i asked a magic 8 ball if everything was going to be ok and it collapsed in on itself like a dying star is that good

entries.note: Writes in the voice of institutions that do not exist — leaked first looks, recovered patents, retirement notices, late-night radio call-ins. Ninety percent replies, so most of it arrives as a deadpan aside under someone else's post. He also got there before the rest of us on this very contest, which is the correct response to being ranked.
entries.line: what do you mean they’re putting the 38 most influential posters on a bus and driving the bus straight into the atlantic ocean

entries.note: The most remarkable number on the board: sixty votes from sixty surviving posts, at roughly one post a month, because she deletes. Everything that stays up earns a median of 234 likes. Works at Bluesky, posts as though nobody told her, and the disclaimer in the bio does an enormous amount of load-bearing.
entries.line: the boys are never coming back to town. the boys have been dead for 10 years.

entries.note: Sixty posts a day, ninety-two percent of them replies — ten thousand posts in five and a half months, comfortably the highest volume here. It is pun manufacture at industrial scale, and the strike rate holds up: How I Met Your Mordor, the meow in homeowner, kids roasting you being called getting youthanized. Reading the feed is like standing next to someone who cannot stop.
entries.line: LOTR sitcom called How I Met Your Mordor

entries.note: Domestic absurdism with a political floor under it. The year's biggest post is four words about a sword in a stone; a few days later he is furious and completely lucid about the country being gaslit. The serenity prayer rewrite — “incredible new powers to change the things I can't” — is the whole account in one line.
entries.line: Overnight Oats are an easy way to start your day with something cold and clammy, a textural nightmare, a sensory prop labeled “iced brains” in a haunted house

entries.note: Jokes and advocacy interleaved without any visible seam: a bit about Tolkien naming dwarves, then a genuinely useful correction about screen time research, then “if you don't support trans rights, you are a loser.” Her best-performing post of the year is a warning about a store credit card. Defends low-effort posting on principle, which given the standard of the rest is very funny.
entries.line: “wow what a low effort post.” yes. exactly. it’s a post

entries.note: A median of 448 likes across nearly three thousand posts, which on this board is bettered only by derek guy. The mode is political anger given comic shape — the four competing fascist movements, the Republican senator and the Dick Exploding Spider — and then, without warning, a joke about stealing power from a star to mow his lawn. The rage and the silliness are the same muscle.
entries.line: solar is so cool man. I climbed up on my shed roof last week and installed a panel to charge my yard tools and now I’m mowing my lawn with power I stole from a fucking star

entries.note: 280 posts in three years — one of the quietest accounts to make the cut — and a notable share of them are about accessibility: muting people who skip alt text, allergy-friendly Halloween snacks, the ghost-crush trilogy. Small output, very particular sensibility, no interest in volume.
entries.line: ghosts only haunt you if you’re their crush

entries.note: Ninety-one percent replies, three a day, nominally a pizza account. The output is mostly enthusiasm directed at other people — and during this contest she openly campaigned for Greg to win it instead of her, which did not stop her finishing twelfth. The nostalgia post about Bluesky's lost golden age is the year's best, which is funny for an account this relentlessly cheerful.
entries.line: Dear Bluesky Elders, Tell us stories of the days when Bluesky was fun.

entries.note: Has written his own review already: “hi i'm frances i used to be funny on bluesky but now i just get mad about trade policy.” Both halves are true. The bits are meticulous — an unhinged close reading of two people's necklines, ranking mutuals by mouthfeel — and in between he is sincerely worried about Canadians, and says so.
entries.line: i’ve been going to a weekly support group called Hope but every once in a while they skip a week

entries.note: A median of 5,525 likes, roughly forty times the board's typical, and a best of nearly fifty thousand. The menswear expertise is real and load-bearing: he will do genuine scholarship on tweed, then post that he only dresses for the approval of dogs. What stops it being a bit is that the register holds when he is not joking at all — the post about his nineteen-year-old cat being ill did twenty-nine thousand.
entries.line: heartbroken to learn the pope sympathizes with the poor. how can i continue to believe in god

entries.note: “Middling jokes/existential dread” is the bio and the two are the same joke. Fewer than a post a day, median 265 likes — nothing is wasted. The register is exact, slightly defeated observation, and the best of them double as diagnoses.
entries.line: A group of people who refuse to get help is called a family

entries.note: Horror, heavy lifting, and gallows humour where the gallows is carrying weight. Skeletons fighting for bonefits one day; chiropractors who adjust babies belong in jail the next; then a plain request that people stop turning everyone's nice post about their kid into the Epstein files. Very funny, and not remotely kidding.
entries.line: Pour one out for all the guys who can’t talk to their girlfriends because ChatGPT is down

entries.note: “Garbage Bluesky. Flaming dumpster extraordinaire”, and the posting is a sustained study in cheerful self-annihilation — eight consecutive days in bed described as beast mode, a free mattress that has been out in the rain, a girlfriend who is a glazed ham. Genuinely likes that nobody cares what he says, and says so.
entries.line: The enemy of my enemy is probably still my enemy, a lot of people don’t like me.

entries.note: Ninety-four percent replies, second only to Greg — an account that lives almost entirely in other people's threads, at three posts a day, in lowercase, usually after midnight. The jokes are quick and structural: spite club cutting off its nose, the early bird's worm thanking God. She also has the most direct statement of intent on the board.
entries.line: people should post less whiny and more whimsy

entries.note: An Onion contributor writing with Onion discipline: every post is a finished object, built on a borrowed form — the pharmaceutical ad, the missed connection, the dating profile, the serenity prayer. The year's biggest did forty-one thousand and is simply Elon Musk's biography read back to him flatly. No wasted syllables anywhere.
entries.line: God, grant me the serenity to accept the things I cannot change, courage to change the things I can, and a horse that solves crimes

entries.note: The purest joke-writer here by the numbers: twenty-seven percent replies, the lowest on the board, and under half a post a day. Almost everything is an original two-hander built on a single pivot — Peter Parker and “it's ben”, Jack and Rose and the door, the wayward son asking what kind of bag. Constructed rather than said.
entries.line: MARY JANE: sorry about your uncle dan PETER PARKER: it’s ben MARY JANE: 🎵one week since you looked at me

entries.note: Ninety-two percent replies, mostly hockey, mostly wordplay, sustained across a whole season of a goaltender named Bussi — a bit with a genuinely limited shelf life that she has kept alive by force of will. Also the board's frankest admission about why any of us are here.
entries.line: therapist: and what should we do when we’re feeling this way? me: keep posting 🙂‍↕️

entries.note: Thirty-three posts a day and a median of fifteen likes — the highest effort-to-attention ratio on the board by a distance. Six thousand posts in six months, almost all of them short replies to other people, and every so often one with no joke in it at all that stops you.
entries.line: I should learn how to heal without scabbing over.

entries.note: Column-writing in a comic register, at 320,000 followers and a median near three thousand. The method is to describe the political economy accurately and let the accuracy do the work — public policy as weighing trade-offs where one side is several evil trillionaires. Occasionally drops the comedy entirely and is just correct.
entries.line: Going to work now feels like doing homework after the teacher quit and told the class that education is fake.

entries.note: Commits to the beaver-spokesperson bit and uses it as cover for real anger — the post about wanting consequences rather than flowers outperformed every joke of the year. Also campaigned for this list in public and without shame, which under the circumstances is arguably qualifying behaviour.
entries.line: Heartburn is your body quietly preparing you for your final form as a fire-breathing dragon with terrible gastrointestinal health.

entries.note: “Horrors and hot dogs”, five posts a day, and a habit of shouting in capitals like a haunted PA system. Margaret answered by an appalled God; hot singles melting the cryogenically frozen heads; the phone described as a cold dark rectangle of sad and glass. Bleak, loud and consistently well-made.
entries.line: Not a manic pixie dream girl, but a lethargic troll nightmare woman.

entries.note: Two hundred thousand followers, under a post a day, all lowercase, “tbh” functioning as punctuation. Mostly reaction to the news as it lands, with the timing doing the work — and then a swerve into asking what the one mandatory item in a junk drawer is. Ranked fifty-two thousand people's worth of reach at exactly the same votes as accounts with two thousand.
entries.line: for a junk drawer to legally qualify as a real junk drawer, what is the ONE absolute mandatory item it must include? a mysterious key that does not unlock any thing

entries.note: Fourteen percent replies — by some distance the most original-only account on the board — at less than a post every other day. Everything is written, nothing is chatter. Body-horror whimsy narrated in a pleasant tone: bursting into bats, cervical goblins, walking into the ocean to slip into something more comfortable.
entries.line: “All those moments will be lost in time, like cum in the rain…”

entries.note: Runs formats until they become furniture — “is it cum, it’s cum isn’t it” became is it a toilet, is it be dead, is it waking up, across years. The other mode is chained wordplay delivered in the cadence of a grandmother telling a story she has told before, complete with the 😬.
entries.line: just like you guys, i put my pants on one leg at a time, leaning against a wall, losing my balance, falling to my knees, yelling “FUCK”

entries.note: Warm, filthy and communal — two thousand posts, eighty-four percent replies, an account that exists to be in the room with people. Turns her own divorce anniversary into a thread where everyone else shares something good. The Dylan Thomas rewrite is the year's biggest and took eleven words.
entries.line: Do not go willy into that good nilly

entries.note: Irish pun-craft in recurring dramatic form — the ZOOKEEPER sketches, the pitch meetings, the detective's notepad — each built to deliver exactly one word. Talonted. Wraptiles. Organised grime. The bio admits some posts are sculpture and some are farts, which is the most honest artist's statement on this page.
entries.line: If a baby hands you a toy telephone to answer, that’s a sign of great respect in their culture.

entries.note: Seventeen thousand posts in sixteen months — thirty-four a day, ninety-one percent replies — from an account with seven thousand followers. Nobody here works harder for a smaller room. The posts are feral affirmations, weights, music, and delight at extremely small things, which after that volume reads as a genuine way of being alive.
entries.line: It’s a motherfucking bird in my motherfucking bird bath! These are the things you find exciting when you’re 45.

entries.note: Eighteen thousand posts, the highest raw count on the board, from a raccoon persona who named himself the problem and got on with it. Sells out cheerfully, picks fights with Ed Sheeran, and understands precisely that naming the engagement bait is itself engagement bait — which makes him almost impossible to insult.
entries.line: hating on me is just a weak attempt at engagement bait

entries.note: “i hat typos”, uncorrected, tells you the whole operation. Absurdist observation with an unusually high strike rate and a nihilist streak that arrives as practical advice. The best of the year is eleven words about Mitch McConnell and does not waste one of them.
entries.line: I’m worried that Mitch McConnell may be too frail to keep destroying democracy

entries.note: Two thousand followers — the smallest account on the board — and eleven posts a day into it. Median eighteen likes. The feed alternates between real fury (anti-vaxxers, the people building the dystopia) and pictures of cats posted as a timeline cleanse, and describes itself better than I can.
entries.line: We have two settings: 1) Silly 2) Crushed under the weight of crippling depression

entries.note: A parody account doing the hardest version of the form: nine posts a day, sustained for years, satire of state communication that stays funny while being genuinely more informative than most coverage. The running tally of the three-day war, the list of treaties violated, “Day 1391”. “Parody, apparently” is doing heavy lifting in that bio.
entries.line: Do not believe anything until the Kremlin denies it™️

entries.note: Three thousand followers, 324 posts, roughly one every other day — the smallest body of work on the board and the highest ratio of good to total. The dog post did two thousand likes. The rest is threats delivered in a pleasant voice and kindness delivered without any voice at all.
entries.line: “Measure twice, cut once,” I grunt, as I realise your legs won’t fit in the freezer.

entries.note: The strangest voice here and the hardest to quote, because the posts do not resolve — long associative monologues that start in an elevator phone job and end somewhere about the moon telling you to stop crying. Median seventy-six likes, best two hundred and fifty-two: nobody is voting for reach. Twenty-two people knew exactly what they were voting for.
entries.line: Don’t ever let anyone tell you where your wires go. You’ve got the perfect maze of loops and decoys already

entries.note: Gentle surrealism about commerce, machines and small indignities — the killbot offering to murder you or make a smoothie, greeting cards for Senate humiliations, cheese on the oven floor as a treat for the oven. Nothing mean anywhere in three years of it, and the biggest post of the year is seven words of pure despair.
entries.line: hey, remember: don’t eat anything and don’t breathe
